chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Al-Fuḍayl, who said:

I asked Abū Al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a thief who entered upon a pregnant woman and fell upon her, so she cast out what was in her womb. Then the woman leapt upon him and killed him. He said: “The blood of the thief is unavenged, and upon the slain man is the blood money for her miscarried fetus.”

key_terms.دِيَةُ سَخْلَتِهَا: the blood money due for her miscarried fetus
key_terms.فَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِي بَطْنِهَا: she miscarried what was in her womb
key_terms.يُطَلُّ دَمُ اللِّصِّ: the thief’s blood is not subject to retaliation or compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a thief assaults a pregnant woman, causes a miscarriage, and is then killed by her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a violent assault on a pregnant woman that resulted in miscarriage and the death of the assailant. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the thief’s blood is not avenged, while liability remains for the diyyah of the miscarried fetus.
